Subject: Private cluster: node/storage constraints + data residency

Hi Karthik / Laura,

Thanks again for taking this initial intake. Attached is an inventory CSV and a rough network diagram for our primary EU site (Frankfurt). High-level asks:

- We need a private Kubernetes cluster in our VPC (no internet egress allowed from model-serving nodes except via a NAT gateway controlled by us).
- Per-tenant logical isolation: customers A/B/C must not share model volumes; we prefer hardware-enforced isolation where feasible.
- Model artifacts are ~6TB in total; active dataset for serving is ~800GB with bursts to 2TB.
- Retention: logs and request traces must be retained for 90 days; audit logs for 1 year.
- Compliance: SOC2 + data residency in EU.

Can you sketch how you’d map node classes and persistent storage (ephemeral vs blockstore vs NFS) and where host-affinity helps reduce egress + startup latency? Also flag anything in the inventory that will block an on-prem install (e.g., IP space, firewall rules, or lack of KMS).

We attached: edgecorp-inventory.csv, network-diagram.pdf

Happy to hop on a 30m call this week.

-Paul

Paul, thanks — good detail in the inventory. Quick availability: we can do a 30m technical intake Thursday 11:00 CET (I’ll send a calendar invite).

A few clarifying Qs before the call so we can come prepared:
- Do you need per-tenant dedicated GPU allocation (true hardware isolation) or is strong tenant node-pinning + taints tolerations acceptable?
- KMS: do you have a customer-managed KMS in Frankfurt (e.g. AWS KMS multi-tenant key or on-prem HSM)? If yes, we’ll outline CMK integration steps.
- Network egress: do you require all outbound model fetches to route through your NAT (no direct internet)? Confirm whether pull-through caching from our hosted registry is allowed or if registry must be hosted on-prem.
- Expected steady-state qps per tenant (token/sec or requests/sec) and typical model sequence length — helps size KV cache and node pool sizing.

I attached our private deployment checklist to help guide the call.

Next steps on our side after the call: a node-profile + storage mapping document and a draft MAP (mutual action plan) for SOW prep.

Thanks,

Subject: Internal: EdgeCorp - preliminary mapping (node classes + storage)

Team, after reviewing EdgeCorp’s inventory and network sketch I recommend the following initial mapping we can present on the call: 

1) Node pools (recommended):
- control-plane (3x m5.large-equivalent, HA) — no GPU, private subnets, restricted SSH;
- infra-utility (2x, for logging/metrics/sidecars) — standard compute, persistent PV for ELK/fluend buffers;
- gpustream (tenant-shared) — GPU nodes with local NVMe for KV cache and ephemeral model loads; use taints/tolerations + nodeAffinity for tenant pinning;
- dedicated-gpu (optional per-tenant commit) — reserved nodes for tenants that purchase HW isolation; encrypted disks;
- storage-proxy (2x) — nodes that act as iSCSI/CSI gateway if blockstore is remote;

2) Storage mapping:
- Model artifacts: blockstore (encrypted RWX) mounted to model-serving pods. For hot models, place on local NVMe and reconcile to blockstore as backing store.
- Persistent logs/traces: append-only NFS or object-store gateway with lifecycle policy (90d); ensure retention policy enforced by sidecar;
- Audit logs: ship to your on-prem S3-compatible archive with 1y retention.

3) Affinity & isolation:
- Use topologySpreadConstraints and soft nodeAffinity to reduce cross-rack egress for model pulls.
- For strict tenancy, we recommend dedicated-gpu nodepool + isolated PV classes bound to that nodepool via NodeFeature discovery labels and CSI topology.

4) Networking & egress:
- All model-fetch traffic must go through your NAT. We’ll add an init-container that verifies fetch endpoints and fail open only to your registry.
- Ensure BGP/eBPF NAT rules allow outbound port ranges for health checks and observability streams.

 blockers/asks for on-prem install:
- KMS/HSM endpoint + credentials for CMK integration;
- NAT IP range and firewall exceptions for the control plane to reach Redwood support endpoints (for telemetry/cert fetching) — we can provide precise IPs during the call;
- CSI credentials for your blockstore/S3-compatible endpoint and a test bucket for audit logs.

If everyone’s aligned I’ll capture this into a short node-profile document and bring to the call.

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Paul Hart <paul.hart@edgecorp.com>

Subject: Re: Private cluster: node/storage constraints + data residency

Karthik — thanks, that mapping is exactly the level of detail we need. Answers inline: 
- Hardware isolation: for Tier-1 tenants we will want dedicated GPU nodepools (budgeted). For Tier-2 we'll accept strong pinning.
- KMS: we have an on-prem HSM reachable from the subnet; we will share operator credentials in the preflight window.
- Registry: must be hosted on-prem. No external registry pulls allowed.
- Steady-state qps: tenant A ~30 rps, tenant B ~8 rps, tenant C ~2 rps. Typical sequence length 512 tokens.
- Logs: we already run an on-prem object store for 90d retention and a tape/archive process for 1y.

Attachments: edgecorp-security-reqs.pdf (SOC2 scoping + audit contact).

For the call, please include someone who can speak to install windows and agent-side telemetry. We’re ready for the canary plan (single-tenant) and a MAP to run through ops handover and runbook.

-Paul
